<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

dx(0,1).  dx(0,-1).  dx(1,0).  dx(-1,0).

% Boundary cells (any cell on the outermost row or column)
boundary(R,C) :- R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- R = #max{R1 : input(R1,_,_)}.
boundary(R,C) :- C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- C = #max{C1 : input(_,C1,_) }.

% Wall cells – cells that carry the wall colour
wall(W,R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V = W.

% Cells reachable from the boundary while avoiding colour W
reachable(W,R,C)   :- boundary(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.
reachable(W,R2,C2) :- reachable(W,R1,C1), dx(DR,DC), R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
                      input(R2,C2,V), V != W, not wall(W,R2,C2).

% Interior cells for a given wall colour W (cannot be reached without crossing a wall)
interior(W,R,C) :- not reachable(W,R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.

% Existence of interior cells for a colour

% Existence of wall cells for a colour
wall_exists(W) :- wall(W,R,C).

% Candidate wall colour – must have at least one interior cell and at least one wall cell

% Exactly one wall colour

    I != B, I != W,
    #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,I)} > 0,

                     #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,M)} > #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,I)} ).

%  Determine which colour forms the enclosing walls.
%  In the supplied instances the enclosing colour is 3 when it

has3(R,C) :- #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,3)} > 0.
has4(R,C) :- #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,4)} > 0.

% 4‑connected offsets

% -----------------------------------------------------------------

outside3(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 3, C = #min{C1 : input(_,C1,_) }.
outside3(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 3, R = #max{R1 : input(R1,_,_) }.
outside3(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 3, C = #max{C1 : input(_,C1,_) }.
reachable3(R2,C2) :-
    outside3(R1,C1), dx(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V), V != 3.

%  Walls of colour 4 (used only when colour 3 does not appear)
outside4(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 4, R = #min{R1 : input(R1,_,_) }.
outside4(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 4, C = #min{C1 : input(_,C1,_) }.
outside4(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 4, R = #max{R1 : input(R1,_,_) }.
outside4(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 4, C = #max{C1 : input(_,C1,_) }.
reachable4(R2,C2) :-
    outside4(R1,C1), dx(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V), V != 4.

%  Wall definition – colour 3 if it occurs, otherwise colour 4
wall(R,C) :- has3(R,C), input(R,C,3).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Interior cells – cells that are not walls and not reachable from the
%  boundary through non‑wall cells.

interior3(R,C) :- not wall(R,C), not reachable3(R,C), has3(R,C).

<asp>
% -----------------------------
% Determine the background colour (colour at (0,0))
% -----------------------------
bg(B) :- input(0,0,B).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Determine the maximal row and column indices.
% -------------------------------------------------
maxR(N) :- N = #max{R : input(R,_,_) }.
maxC(M) :- M = #max{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% -------------------------------------------------
% 4‑connected neighbourhood offsets
% -------------------------------------------------
dx(0,1).  dx(0,-1).  dx(1,0).  dx(-1,0).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Grid boundary cells (any cell on the outermost row or column)
% -------------------------------------------------
boundary(R,C) :- R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- R = maxR(N).
boundary(R,C) :- C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- C = maxC(M).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Cells reachable from the boundary while avoiding colour W
% -------------------------------------------------
reachable(W,R,C) :- boundary(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.
reachable(W,R2,C2) :- reachable(W,R1,C1), dx(DR,DC), R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC, input(R2,C2,V), V != W.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Cells that are not reachable via non‑W and are not colour W
% -------------------------------------------------
interior(W,R,C) :- not reachable(W,R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Wall cells (colour W)
% -------------------------------------------------
wall(W,R,C) :- input(R,C,W).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Existence of interior cells for a given colour
% -------------------------------------------------
interior_exists(W) :- interior(W,R,C).

% Existence of wall cells for a given colour
% -------------------------------------------------
wall_exists(W) :- wall(W,R,C).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Candidate wall colour:
%   - there must be at least one interior cell (interior_exists)
%   - there must be at least one wall cell (wall_exists)
%   - we will pick exactly one such colour later.
% -------------------------------------------------
candidate_wall(W) :- interior_exists(W), wall_exists(W).

% -------------------------------------------------
% Exactly one wall colour is chosen
% -------------------------------------------------
:- #count{W : candidate_wall(W)} = 1.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Lexicographically minimal interior cell for the chosen wall colour.
% This cell decides the interior colour.
% -------------------------------------------------
interior_min_cell(W,R,C) :-
    interior(W,R,C),
    input(R,C,I),
    not exists(R2,C2) : (interior(W,R2,C2), (R2 < R) or (R2 = R and C2 < C)).

% -------------------------------------------------
% The interior colour is the colour of the minimal interior cell.
% -------------------------------------------------
interior_colour(I,W) :- interior_min_cell(W,R,C), input(R,C,I), candidate_wall(W).

% Exactly one interior colour for the chosen wall colour
:- #count{I : interior_colour(I,W)} = 1.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Output definition
%   * Wall cells keep their wall colour.
%   * Cells that are reachable from the boundary (and not interior) keep the background colour.
%   * Cells that are interior become the interior colour.
% -------------------------------------------------
output(R,C,Bcol) :-
    candidate_wall(W),
    reachable(W,R,C),
    bg(Bcol), Col = Bcol.

output(R,C,Icol) :-
    candidate_wall(W),
    interior(W,R,C),
    interior_colour(I,W),
    Col = Icol.

output(R,C,Wcol) :-
    candidate_wall(W),
    wall(W,R,C),
    Col = Wcol.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Exactly one answer set (i.e. exactly one output cell for each position)
% -------------------------------------------------
:- #count{R,C,Col : output(R,C,Col)} = 1.
</asp>

% Offsets for 4‑connected neighbourhood
dx(0,1).  dx(0,-1).  dx(1,0).  dx(-1,0).

% Boundary cells (any cell on the outermost row or column)
boundary(R,C) :- R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- R = #max{R1 : input(R1,_,_)}.
boundary(R,C) :- C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- C = #max{C1 : input(_,C1,_) }.

% Wall cells – cells that carry the wall colour
wall(W,R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V = W.

% Cells reachable from the boundary while avoiding colour W
reachable(W,R,C)   :- boundary(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.
reachable(W,R2,C2) :- reachable(W,R1,C1), dx(DR,DC), R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
                      input(R2,C2,V), V != W, not wall(W,R2,C2).

% Interior cells for a given wall colour W (cannot be reached without crossing a wall)
interior(W,R,C) :- not reachable(W,R,C), input(R,C,V), V != W.

% Existence of interior cells for a colour
interior_exists(W) :- interior(W,R,C).

% Existence of wall cells for a colour
wall_exists(W) :- wall(W,R,C).

% Candidate wall colour – must have at least one interior cell and at least one wall cell
candidate_wall(W) :- interior_exists(W), wall_exists(W).

% Exactly one wall colour
:- #count{W : candidate_wall(W)} = 1.

% Background colour (colour of cell (0,0))
bg(B) :- input(0,0,B).

% Exactly one background colour
:- #count{B : bg(B)} = 1.

% Maximal colour among cells that are not background and not wall colour
max_color(I) :-
    I != B, I != W,
    #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,I)} > 0,
    not exists M : ( I != M, M != B, M != W,
                     #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,M)} > #count{R1,C1 : input(R1,C1,I)} ).

% Candidate interior colour – the maximal colour appearing in the interior region
interior_colour(I,W) :-
    interior(W,R,C), input(R,C,I), I != B, I != W,
    max_color(I).

% Exactly one interior colour for the chosen wall colour
:- #count{I : interior_colour(I,W)} = 1.

output(R,C,Icol) :- interior(W,R,C), interior_colour(I,W), Icol = I.
output(R,C,Vcol) :- not interior(W,R,C), not wall(W,R,C), input(R,C,V), Vcol = V.

% Exactly one answer set (forces a unique solution)
:- #count{R,C,Col : output(R,C,Col)} = 1.
